top_categories.workout_context: Krk Gran Fondo's rolling island roads forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 51 miles.
51 miles on rolling island roads burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Krk Gran Fondo's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before April.
When someone attacks on rolling island roads, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
85ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
Base fitness for Krk Gran Fondo. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Krk Gran Fondo, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
At Krk Gran Fondo, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Krk Gran Fondo. Train it until it feels boring.
Short, max efforts are unavoidable. Punchy climbs, gap closures, attacks on rolling island roads. If you haven't trained them, you'll crack.
Varied gradients on rolling island roads demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
Smooth pedaling at 51 miles saves muscle. Bad technique at mile 10 is invisible. At mile 80 it's a cramp.

race_overlay.heat: April in Punat, Island of Krk, Primorje-Gorski Kotar County, Croatia can bring heat. If the forecast warrants it, include controlled heat exposure before Krk Gran Fondo and rehearse the drinking and electrolyte plan you tolerate in training. Do not introduce a fixed sodium protocol solely from this preview.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 40–60g carbs/hour for Krk Gran Fondo’s 51 miles. Front-load calories in the first half. One bottle per hour minimum, more in heat.
race_overlay.altitude: Moderate altitude at Krk Gran Fondo. Arrive 2–3 days early. Reduce intensity expectations by 5–10%. Hydrate aggressively.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at Krk Gran Fondo requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on rolling island roads to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Road Specific, Durability, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 51 miles of rolling island roads in Punat, Island of Krk, Primorje-Gorski Kotar County, Croatia.
